title: an sgo.select2 arm that assigns to an enclosing var emits scala.runtime.BooleanRef, which the Go backend has no type mapping for — the compile dies after typing, at emit
body:
REPRO SURFACE: wata-watch src/main/scala/nsurlsession.scala (plan 0075), first draft of NsHttp.doSend:

    var timedOut = false
    sgo.select2(doneCh, go.time.After(go.time.milliseconds(timeoutMs.toInt)))(
      (_b: Boolean) => (), () => timedOut = true)
    if timedOut then ...

sgola types it fine and then fails with:

  sgola spike: no Go type mapping for `scala.runtime.BooleanRef` — missing stdlib surface (shim-addressable, not a restriction):
  sgola has not grown this type. If this is a function type, only def params and case-class fields recover `func(...)` shapes; a function-typed module val / local var annotation is unsupported.

So the var-capture lowering reaches for the Scala 2-style IntRef/BooleanRef box classes, which are JVM-runtime artifacts with no Go mapping. The error message itself says 'shim-addressable': either (a) map BooleanRef/IntRef/&co to tiny emitted Go structs (a single-field box), or (b) — better — lower captured-var mutation in lambda bodies to a one-element array or an emitter-internal cell the way sgo.Atomic already lowers, or (c) reject at TYPING time with a fix-menu pointing at the supported spelling, so this is a loud restriction instead of a post-type crash.

WHY IT MATTERS: select2's arms are single-statement by ruling, so 'select over {work, timer} and remember which fired' is THE idiom for a synchronous FFI wait (wata-watch's NSURLSession HttpDo waits out a data task against a deadline). Every consumer will write exactly this first draft. The spec already forbids non-local return inside anonymous functions; arm-body var mutation is adjacent and currently fails late and cryptically.

WORKAROUND (shipped, keep-or-improve is your call): a module-level sgo.Atomic[Boolean] that the producing side sets before sending the completion token; the waiter reads it after select2 returns. Emitted Go is clean (atomic.Bool). It costs a second shared cell per wait and puts the ordering burden ('set flag BEFORE send') on the caller — a selectValue-over-two-channels spelling, or select2 arms allowed to PRODUCE a discriminated value (an Either-like result), would delete the workaround.
